name: Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport
before:
Zimbabwe's largest airport and the base for Air Zimbabwe, serving Harare.

The names are a problem for searching. It is now Robert Gabriel Mugabe International, is widely called Harare Airport or just RGM, and was previously Harare International and before that Salisbury Airport. Older supplier records may use any of them, and its ICAO code changed from FVHA to FVRG.

The airport was commissioned in 1956 and opened on 5 February 1957, replacing Belvedere Airport, whose runway was badly aligned. Aircraft had to approach through a gap in the Warren Hills and take off over the city centre, which was dangerous, and the growing number of tall buildings made it worse.

The Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe has its head office on level 3 of the international terminal.
after:
Zimbabwe's largest airport, serving the capital, Harare. It is run by the Airports Company of Zimbabwe.

The official name is Robert Gabriel Mugabe International Airport. Its name until November 2017 was Harare International Airport, so older supplier records may still use that name. It began as Salisbury Airport in 1956. The ICAO code is FVRG, though some databases still carry the old code, FVHA.

Air Zimbabwe, the national airline, resumed direct flights from Harare to London Gatwick in July 2026, flown for it by the Spanish airline Plus Ultra.

The FCDO warns of smash-and-grab robberies from vehicles at the main intersections on the route to the airport.

claims.claim: resumed direct flights Harare to London Gatwick in July 2026, flown by Plus Ultra
claims.inAfter: resumed direct flights from Harare to London Gatwick in July 2026, flown for it by the Spanish airline Plus Ultra
claims.note: Added: the most important change for a UK agent, and the subject of the FCDO's latest update. Dates differ in detail (Aviation Week: the wet lease starts 1 July; the FCDO said 'has resumed' in its 15 July update; Air Zimbabwe gives 22 July as the resumption date), so only the month is given. Air Zimbabwe says three flights a week and an A330-300, Aviation Week an A330-200, so neither the frequency nor the aircraft is stated. Air Zimbabwe says the return flights use Gatwick's South Terminal; one source, not stated.

claims.wasBefore: and the base for Air Zimbabwe
claims.why: Only Wikipedia says 'base' in so many words. Air Zimbabwe's about page does not, and its contact page was down (Sucuri 502, twice). Its own pages do show its London and domestic flights starting in Harare, which the new text says instead.

claims.claim: widely called Harare Airport or just RGM
claims.wasBefore: is widely called Harare Airport or just RGM
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. The operator writes 'RG Mugabe Int. Airport' and the aviation authority's 2017 notice 'R. G. Mugabe International Airport', neither 'RGM'. The Zimbabwean papers that use the nicknames (Herald, Chronicle, Sunday Mail, ZBC, ZimLive) answer with a Cloudflare challenge and NewsDay refused the request.

claims.claim: commissioned 1956, opened 5 February 1957, replacing Belvedere Airport
claims.wasBefore: The airport was commissioned in 1956 and opened on 5 February 1957, replacing Belvedere Airport, whose runway was badly aligned.
claims.why: The 1956 start is kept with the operator. The 5 February 1957 opening and the Belvedere story rest on Wikipedia alone: the 1957 Flight report and the University of Zimbabwe paper it cites are reachable only through web.archive.org, which the network policy blocks.

claims.wasBefore: Aircraft had to approach through a gap in the Warren Hills and take off over the city centre, which was dangerous, and the growing number of tall buildings made it worse.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (from a 1950 report it paraphrases), and history of no use for booking.

claims.claim: Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe head office on level 3
claims.wasBefore: The Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe has its head office on level 3 of the international terminal.
claims.why: Out of date or at least unconfirmed. The airport has been run since the 2018 Act by the Airports Company of Zimbabwe, which gives its OWN head office as '3rd Level, Int. Terminal Building'; nothing current places the Civil Aviation Authority there, and its site (caaz.co.zw) dropped the connection. Replaced by who runs the airport.
